evidence.reference_title: Knock-in human GDF5 proregion L373R mutation as a mouse model for proximal symphalangism.
evidence.snippet: The variant also caused upregulation of SMAD1/5/8 phosphorylation and increased expression of target genes SMURF1, along with COL2A1 and SOX9 which are factors associated with chondrosis.

evidence.reference_title: Cushing proximal symphalangism and the NOG and GDF5 genes.
evidence.snippet: too little expression of NOG, a growth antagonist, or overexpression of GDF5, a growth agonist, results in cartilage overgrowth and bony fusion.

nodes.description: The joint interzone between adjacent phalanges, and between some tarsal bones, does not form or is not maintained. The cartilage elements stay continuous and ossify as one, giving bony fusion of the proximal interphalangeal joint and tarsal coalition. In knock-in mice carrying the p.Leu373Arg equivalent, embryonic joint development is abnormal and the phalanx joints are stiff and adherent.

evidence.reference_title: Knock-in human GDF5 proregion L373R mutation as a mouse model for proximal symphalangism.
evidence.snippet: It was also confirmed the joint formation and development was abnormal in Gdf5L367R/+ and Gdf5L367R/L367R mice, including the failure to develop the primary ossification center and be hypertrophic chondrocytes during embryonic development.

evidence.snippet: In one family with SYM1, we found a novel missense mutation, c.1118T > G (p.L373R), which changes a highly conserved amino acid in the prodomain of GDF5.

evidence.reference_title: Recurrent missense mutation of GDF5 (p.R438L) causes proximal symphalangism in a British family.
evidence.snippet: Genetic testing in the eldest child and his mother identified a heterozygous missense mutation in GDF5 c.1313G>T (p.R438L), thereby establishing SYM1B as the cause of the orthopaedic problems in this family.

nodes.description: The SYM1B variants make GDF5 more active rather than less. p.Arg438Leu, in the receptor-binding surface of the mature ligand, keeps normal binding to BMPR1B and to noggin but gains binding to BMPR1A, the receptor normally used by BMP2, so the ligand acquires BMP2-like activity. p.Leu373Arg, in the prodomain, increases proteolytic release of the mature ligand. p.Glu491Lys alters a conserved residue of the mature domain; its biochemical effect has not been described in the cited sources.

evidence.reference_title: Activating and deactivating mutations in the receptor interaction site of GDF5 cause symphalangism or brachydactyly type A2.
evidence.snippet: the R438L mutant showed normal binding to BMPR1B but increased binding to BMPR1A, the receptor normally activated by BMP2. The binding to NOGGIN was normal for both mutants.

evidence.reference_title: Activating and deactivating mutations in the receptor interaction site of GDF5 cause symphalangism or brachydactyly type A2.
evidence.snippet: the symphalangism phenotype (R438L) is caused by a loss of receptor-binding specificity, resulting in a gain of function by the acquisition of BMP2-like properties.
